title: A-10 aircraft hit by Iranian air defenses, second US aircraft to go down in the Middle East
byline: A US official confirmed that a second aircraft went down in the Middle East on Friday. The official spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitive military situation.

title: Tehran rejected 48-hour ceasefire proposal from US, Iranian media, citing source, says
byline: An unnamed source told Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency on Friday that Tehran had ⁠rejected a U.S. proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire.

title: Eight dead after earthquake of magnitude 5.9 strikes Afghanistan
byline: Eight people were killed and one child was injured on Friday when a house collapsed in Kabul following an earthquake in Afghanistan, the National Disaster Management Authority said.

title: Greece reshuffles Cabinet after ministers resign over farm subsidy scandal
byline: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis reshuffled his Cabinet Friday after three ministers resigned earlier in the day amid a widening farm subsidies scandal.

title: Fairly heavy showers expected in several parts of the island
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in most parts of the island after 1.00 p.m. today (04), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: GMOA resumes island-wide strike from today
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) announced that it has resumed an island-wide strike from 8 a.m. today (04).

title: Trump proposes “historic” defense spending budget, eyes 10% cut to other federal programs
byline: President Donald Trump on Friday requested a 10% cut in non-defense spending for the 2027 fiscal year and a massive $500 billion increase in the military budget, as the U.S. continues its war against Iran.

title: Details of scheduled water cuts in Colombo District today
byline: The scheduled water cuts affecting several areas in the Colombo District, due to prevailing dry weather conditions, will continue today (April 04).

title: 16-year-old boy drowns while bathing in canal at Perathuweli
byline: A 16-year-old boy, a resident of the Perathuweli area, has tragically died after drowning in a canal within the Kantale police division.

title: ‘1990 Suwa Seriya’ ambulance service’s new head office inaugurated
byline: The new head office of the ‘1990 Suwa Seriya’ Ambulance Service was officially inaugurated today (April 4) under the patronage of the Minister of Health and Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa.

title: Ship with 25,000 MT of fertilizer scheduled to arrive tomorrow – Dy Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Namal Karunaratne, stated that a ship carrying 25,000 metric tons of fertilizer is scheduled to arrive in the country tomorrow (April 5).

title: AI-generated ‘Fruit Love Island’ takes TikTok by storm
byline: Millions of people have been gripped by the juicy twists of an AI-generated TikTok micro-series based on the television hit “Love Island” -- except all the participants are sexy human-like fruit.

title: First Japanese and French ships cross Strait of Hormuz since war
byline: One French- and another Japanese-owned vessel are among a handful of vessels to have crossed the war-torn Strait of Hormuz, maritime tracking data showed Friday.

title: Association of Medical Specialists not supporting GMOA’s strike
byline: The Association of Medical Specialists (AMS) stated that they will not support the strike action launched this morning (April 4) by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA).

title: Two teens killed in motorcycle accident in Kilinochchi
byline: Two 19-year-old boys have died in a motorcycle accident that occurred in the Dharmapuram area of Kilinochchi.

title: One dead, 47 injured after ‘incident’ at Peru football derby
byline: At least one person died and 47 more were injured Friday night in an unspecified “incident” at Alejandro Villanueva Stadium in Peru’s capital during a rally ahead of a football derby, according to the health ministry.

title: Telegram’s Durov says Russia triggered payment system problem by blocking VPNs
byline: Telegram founder Pavel Durov said on Saturday Russia’s attempt to block Virtual Private Networks triggered a problem with a domestic payment system, adding that tens of millions of ⁠Russians were now resisting the digital controls.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Central, Sabaragamuwa, Uva, Southern, Eastern and Northcentral provinces, and Vavuniya and Mullaittivu districts.

title: Govt spends over Rs. 6 million to train a doctor – Minister
byline: The government spends more than Rs. 6 million of public funds to train a single doctor in Sri Lanka, the Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment, Dr. Upali Pannilage stated.

title: 20 illegally assembled vehicles linked to organized crime seized
byline: Three suspects have been arrested by police along with 20 vehicles, including recently assembled luxury vehicles that were illegally put together.

title: Colombo water cut duration reduced
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board has announced a reduction in the duration of water cuts to Padukka, Homagama, Pelanwatta and Pannipitiya from tomorrow (05).

title: GMOA decides to continue its ongoing token strike
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has announced that it will continue its island-wide token strike beyond 8:00 a.m. tomorrow (05).

title: Colombo water cut duration to be further reduced - NWSDB
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) says that it is paying attention to further reducing the duration of scheduled water cuts in several areas of Colombo.

title: UN Security Council postpones vote on Strait of Hormuz
byline: The UN Security Council is now expected to vote next week on a Bahraini resolution to secure transit passage in the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported on Friday, citing diplomats.

title: Sajith Premadasa attended Gammanpila’s book launch amid AI controversy, Mujibur confirms
byline: The Leader of Opposition, Sajith Premadasa attended the launch of book “Searching for the Mastermind of the Easter Sunday Attacks”, authored by Udaya Gammanpila, the leader of the of the Pivithuru Hela Urumaya (PHU), confirmed Samagi Jana Balawegaya Parliamentarian Mujibur Rahman confirmed today (04).

title: Health Minister challenges GMOA over ‘baseless’ strike
byline: The strike launched by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) against the appointment system for doctors who have completed their internship lacks any basis for discussion, the Minister of Health and Mass Media, Nalinda Jayatissa has stated.

title: India makes first Iranian oil buy in seven years with no payment problems
byline: Indian refiners have purchased Iranian oil amid the Middle East conflict that has disrupted supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, the oil ministry said on Saturday.

title: Area near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant attacked again
byline: Iran’s atomic agency says an airstrike has hit near its Bushehr nuclear facility, killing a security guard and damaging a support building.

title: 96% of recent medical graduates apply for post-internship appointments – Health Ministry
byline: Around 96% of medical graduates who recently completed their internship have applied for post-internship appointments, the Ministry of Health stated.

title: Iraqi border crossing with Iran closed following deadly airstrike
byline: A border crossing connecting Iraq with Iran has been targeted in an airstrike, with Iran’s state-run news agency Tasnim reporting one Iraqi civilian was killed in the attack.

title: Even after Iran war ends, restoring global economy will take two years or more – Analyst
byline: Political analyst Dr Tudor Weerasinghe has warned that ongoing military conflicts in the Middle East could have severe repercussions for Sri Lanka and other Asian countries.

title: Iran has 48 hours to make a deal before ‘hell will reign down’, Trump says
byline: US President Donald Trump says Iran has 48 hours to “make a deal” or open the Strait of Hormuz before “Hell will reign [sic] down on them”.

title: Landslide warnings issued to two DS areas in Ratnapura
byline: Landslide warnings have been issued to two Divisional Secretariat divisions in the Ratnapura District following heavy rainfall in the area.

title: Magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes off north Indonesia: USGS
byline: A 6.0 magnitude quake struck off Indonesia’s remote northern Talaud islands on Saturday (Apr 4), the US Geological Survey (USGS) said, with no immediate reports of casualties or damage.

title: Fire breaks out on main island of Castlereagh Reservoir
byline: A fire broke out this afternoon (April 4) on the main island of the Castlereagh Reservoir, a key source of water for national electricity generation.

title: More than 30 Iranian universities have faced “direct attacks,” Minister says
byline: Iran’s science minister said more than 30 Iranian universities have faced “direct attacks” so far during the war with the US and Israel, according to the state-aligned Iran Students’ News Agency.

title: Northern Railway Line to fully resume operations from Apr. 9
byline: The Department of Railways has completed restoration work on the Northern Railway Line, which was damaged by Cyclone Ditwah last year.

title: More than 1,400 people have been killed in Lebanon since March 2
byline: The number of people who have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon has surpassed 1,400, according to an update shared by the Lebanese health ministry a short while ago.

title: Water cut in Homagama reduced to 12 hours – NWSDB
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has decided to reduce the duration of the scheduled water cut to 12 hours.

title: Grade 11 student missing after drowning in Kehelgamu Oya
byline: A schoolboy has gone missing after reportedly drowning in the Kehelgamu Oya, a tributary that feeds into the Castlereagh Reservoir.

title: Niece of slain IRGC commander Qasem Soleimani to be deported from US
byline: The niece of Qasem Soleimani, a high-ranking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander who was killed by the US in 2020, has been arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement along with her daughter, with both facing deportation, the State Department announced today.
